title: LegeOS project
description: A project session: the files, applications, directories and environment a person works in, instead of a numbered virtual desktop. Mirrors lege_session_core::projects::Project, and is the payload of Projects1.Describe and Projects1.ListDetailed. Stored as one JSON blob and read additively in both directions: an older binary ignores keys it does not know, and a newer one defaults keys an older writer omitted.

directories.description: Further directories that belong to the project, beyond the root.

apps.description: The applications the project remembers, restored when it opens.

app_id.description: The variant to launch when no logical app is recorded, or the variant the logical app resolved to when it was added.

logical_app.description: The logical application, when the project remembers one. Preferred over app_id at open time, so a project survives the Flatpak replacing the package.

last_variant.description: The variant that actually launched last time. Recorded so the project reopens what the person was using, not merely what is default today.

last_instance.description: The instance id from the last open, if it is still meaningful.

checkpoint_token.description: Opaque token the application returned when it was checkpointed.

environment.description: Environment variables applied to applications the project launches.

terminal_directories.description: Where terminals opened in this project start.

mounts.description: Filesystems the project expects to be present.

references.description: Things the project points at that are not its own files: a URL, a document elsewhere, an issue tracker. Kept as opaque strings — the project is a place to work, not a link database.

importance.description: Two values, because a person can honestly answer 'does this one matter more than the others' and cannot honestly answer 'is this a 7 or an 8'. An Important project that is open asks the resource governor to protect the applications it launched; closing it, or demoting it, hands them back.

state.description: An archived project is out of the way, not gone: it stays searchable and it still opens.

created_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the project was created.

updated_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the last change to the project itself.

last_opened_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the last Open. Zero (or absent) means never.

$comment: Projects1.Update accepts a partial object of the user-editable keys only: name, root, directories, environment, terminal_directories, mounts, references, importance, state. `id`, `apps` and the timestamps are owned by the daemon and are refused rather than ignored.
